newsitem.title: UK: Exco says 1997 start means continued caution.
newsitem.headline: Exco says 1997 start means continued caution.

text.p: Wholesale securities broking group Exco Plc said on Wednesday that the first two months of 1997 have indicated the need for continued caution in its outlook.

"Unpredictability is an inherent characteristic of our markets and it is too early to anticipate the outcome for the year," chairman David Hubbard said in a statement. "However the first two months trading indicates the need for continued caution.
Earlier, Exco reported virtually flat 1996 pre-tax profits of 18.2 million stg and announced a full year dividend of 4.5p compared to 9.0p in the previous year.
After a good first quarter in 1996, Exco said that volumes had declined and commission rates had again come under pressure.
Exco shares were 1.5p lower at 61.5p at 1215 GMT.
Hubbard said Exco would continue to increase its exposure to products and markets with good profit potential while withdrawing from more mature ones with limited scope for growth.

It said it will focus on securities, derivatives, capital markets and interest rate products and will reduce its presence in markets like spot foreign exchange where there is over-capacity and thin margins.
Exco said it will make further efforts to drive down fixed costs after cutting the cost base by 17 million stg in 1996.
It said further action is underway including a programme to cut the cost of the Group's international telecommunications system.
